title: Talking About Your Weekend and Free Time

vocabulary.meaning_en: free time when you are not working
vocabulary.example: What do you do in your leisure time?

vocabulary.meaning_en: an activity you do for fun
vocabulary.example: Reading is my favourite pastime.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) do (often used in questions about free time)
vocabulary.note_ar: What did you get up to? = ماذا فعلت؟
vocabulary.note_en: What did you get up to? = What did you do?
vocabulary.example: What did you get up to at the weekend?

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) spend time somewhere doing nothing special
vocabulary.example: We just hung about with some friends.

vocabulary.meaning_en: giving you satisfaction or a good feeling
vocabulary.example: Coaching children is really rewarding.

vocabulary.meaning_en: taking a lot of time
vocabulary.example: Being on the club committee is very time-consuming.

vocabulary.meaning_en: producing good results; useful
vocabulary.example: It was a fruitful weekend in the countryside.

vocabulary.meaning_en: making a lot of money
vocabulary.example: Selling old watches can be lucrative.

vocabulary.meaning_en: so interesting that it takes all your attention
vocabulary.example: I find a good detective novel very absorbing.

vocabulary.meaning_en: boring and ordinary
vocabulary.example: Sport gets me away from my humdrum routine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) a person who loves museums, galleries and theatre
vocabulary.example: My sister is a real culture vulture.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) a person who sits watching TV a lot
vocabulary.meaning_ar: شخص كسول يلازم الأريكة ويشاهد التلفاز
vocabulary.example: Don't be a couch potato. Let's go for a walk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who does a little of many activities
vocabulary.meaning_ar: شخص يجرّب أنشطة كثيرة بشكل سطحي
vocabulary.example: He's a dabbler: a bit of painting, a bit of photography.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an active person who likes doing things
vocabulary.example: She never sits still. She's a real doer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: liking something (not as strong as love)
vocabulary.example: He's fond of football.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) liking something so much you can't stop
vocabulary.example: He's completely hooked on golf.

vocabulary.meaning_en: loving something very much
vocabulary.example: She's passionate about reading.

vocabulary.meaning_en: try something for the first time
vocabulary.example: I've never skied, but I'll have a go.

vocabulary.meaning_en: start a new hobby or activity
vocabulary.example: I took up cycling last year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: do-it-yourself: making or repairing things at home yourself
vocabulary.example: My brother likes doing DIY.

fine_lines.title: play vs do vs go
fine_lines.explanation_ar: play مع الرياضات الجماعية والألعاب بالكرة (play football). do مع الهوايات والأنشطة الفردية (do DIY, do judo). go مع الأنشطة المنتهية بـ ing (go swimming, go fishing).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Play" for team sports and ball games (play football). "Do" for hobbies and individual activities (do DIY, do judo). "Go" for activities ending in -ing (go swimming, go fishing).

examples.sentence: He plays tennis with his colleagues.
My brother does DIY at the weekend.
I like to go cycling on Saturdays.

fine_lines.title: like to vs like + -ing
fine_lines.explanation_ar: يقول هاري إنه لا يوجد فرق حقيقي في المعنى بين I like to swim وI like swimming. وكذلك hate.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Harry says there is really no difference between "I like to swim" and "I like swimming". The same is true for "hate".

examples.sentence: I like to go to the cinema at the weekend.
I like going to the cinema at the weekend.

fine_lines.title: fond of → into → hooked on / passionate about
fine_lines.explanation_ar: fond of = يحبه بشكل معتدل. into = يحبه كثيرًا. hooked on = لا يستطيع التوقف عنه (غير رسمية). passionate about = شغوف به بعمق.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Fond of" = like it. "Into" = like it a lot. "Hooked on" = can't stop (informal). "Passionate about" = love it deeply.

expressions.phrase: What did you do at the weekend?
expressions.meaning_ar: ماذا فعلت في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟
expressions.example: Hi, Sam. What did you do at the weekend?

expressions.phrase: What did you get up to last weekend?
expressions.meaning_ar: ماذا فعلت في عطلة الأسبوع الماضي؟
expressions.meaning_en: An informal question about the weekend.
expressions.example: So, what did you get up to last weekend?

expressions.phrase: Are you getting up to anything this weekend?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل لديك شيء تفعله في عطلة هذا الأسبوع؟
expressions.example: Are you getting up to anything this weekend?

expressions.meaning_ar: هل لديك خطط لعطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟

expressions.phrase: We just hung about with some friends.
expressions.meaning_ar: قضينا الوقت مع بعض الأصدقاء فقط.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you had a relaxed weekend with friends.
expressions.example: Nothing special. We just hung about with some friends.
On Sunday we visited the old folks.

expressions.meaning_en: Says you didn't do anything special.
expressions.example: What did you do? — Nothing much. I stayed home.

expressions.meaning_en: Says an activity gives you satisfaction.
expressions.example: I coach a children's team. It's really rewarding.

expressions.meaning_en: Says something takes a lot of time.
expressions.example: Golf is fun, but it's very time-consuming.

expressions.meaning_en: Says something holds all your attention.
Says someone watches TV all the time.
expressions.example: He watches TV all weekend. He's a real couch potato.

expressions.meaning_en: Says someone loves museums and exhibitions.
expressions.example: She visits every new exhibition. She's a real culture vulture.

expressions.meaning_en: Says someone does a bit of an activity.
Says you like something a lot.
expressions.example: I'm really into hiking at the moment.
I've never been skiing, but I'll have a go.

expressions.meaning_en: Says when you started a hobby.
expressions.example: I took up swimming last year.

expressions.phrase: I don't socialise as much as I'd like.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أختلط بالناس بالقدر الذي أريده.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you don't go out with people often.
expressions.example: With the new baby, I don't socialise as much as I'd like.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency
grammar.explanation_ar: always / usually / sometimes / rarely / never توضع قبل الفعل الرئيسي وبعد فعل be. تقول كم مرة تفعل شيئًا.
grammar.explanation_en: always / usually / sometimes / rarely / never go before the main verb and after "be". They say how often you do something.
examples: I always go cycling on Saturdays.
I sometimes play golf with my father.
I usually go to the gym twice a week.

grammar.title: play / do / go + activity
grammar.explanation_ar: play + رياضة جماعية أو لعبة. do + هواية أو نشاط فردي. go + نشاط بـ ing.
grammar.explanation_en: play + team sport or game; do + hobby or individual activity; go + activity in -ing.
examples: We go fishing in the summer.

grammar.title: Prepositions after leisure adjectives
grammar.explanation_ar: fond of، into، hooked on، passionate about. بعد حرف الجر نستخدم اسمًا أو فعلًا بـ ing.
grammar.explanation_en: fond of, into, hooked on, passionate about. After the preposition use a noun or -ing.
examples: I'm hooked on this puzzle game.
